info.title: QwkSearch Research Agent API
info.description:
API for QwkSearch — AI-powered research with search, extraction, chat, document management, and multi-provider LLM support.

## Authentication

- **Public endpoints** work without credentials. When a deployment sets `REQUIRE_API_KEY`, they need an API key, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `X-API-Key: <key>`.
- **Research-agent endpoints** (`/agent/*` chats, messages, history) accept either a signed-in session or the user's API key, so embedding sites can act for a linked user.
- **Account endpoints** (`/user/*`, `/notebooklm/*`, `/admin/*`) need a signed-in session cookie.

Sign-in itself is served by Better Auth under `/auth/*`; partner sites link an account with the "Sign in with QwkSearch" flow under `/connect/*`.

apiKey.description: Your QwkSearch API key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Find it under Settings → Account. On the public endpoints a key is only checked when the deployment requires one; on the research-agent endpoints it signs you in as the key's owner (chats, history, plan-gated models).

apiKeyHeader.name: X-API-Key
apiKeyHeader.description: The same API key, sent as an `X-API-Key` header instead of `Authorization`.

sessionCookie.name: better-auth.session_token
sessionCookie.description: A signed-in browser session (Better Auth; `__Secure-better-auth.session_token` over HTTPS). Account management — profile, password, sessions, deletion — accepts only this, never an API key, so a leaked key cannot take over the account.

googleDriveCookie.name: google_access_token
googleDriveCookie.description: Google OAuth tokens set by the `/doc/google-docs/auth` → `/doc/google-docs/callback` flow (`google_access_token`, refreshed from `google_refresh_token`).
